task_description:
# Appwrite Storage: Create a Secure Uploads Bucket

## Background
Appwrite Storage organizes files into buckets. Each bucket can enforce file size limits, allowed extensions, compression, encryption, virus scanning, and per-file or per-bucket permissions. Your team needs a hardened bucket called `secure-uploads` that only authenticated users can access, with a strict size/extension policy and storage-side protections enabled.

You will write a Node.js script (using the official `node-appwrite` Server SDK) that creates this bucket against a real Appwrite project. The Appwrite endpoint, project ID, and API key are provided via environment variables.

## Requirements
- Create a new Storage bucket using `storage.createBucket` with all of the following settings:
  - `permissions`: grant read AND write access to any signed-in user (use `Role.users()`).
  - `fileSecurity`: `true` (per-file permissions enabled).
  - `maximumFileSize`: `5242880` bytes (exactly 5 MiB).
  - `allowedFileExtensions`: `["jpg", "jpeg", "png", "webp"]` (order does not matter; values must be exactly these four).
  - `compression`: `"gzip"`.
  - `encryption`: `true`.
  - `antivirus`: `true`.
- Use the bucket name `secure-uploads-${run-id}` (see `run-id` rules below). The bucket display name and the bucket ID must both incorporate the `run-id` suffix.
- After creation, print the newly created bucket's ID to standard output as the LAST non-empty line, in the format: `BUCKET_ID: <bucket_id>`.

## Implementation Hints
- Install/use the `node-appwrite` Server SDK. The SDK exposes `Client`, `Storage`, `ID`, `Permission`, and `Role`.
- Read `APPWRITE_ENDPOINT`, `APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID`, and `APPWRITE_API_KEY` from environment variables to configure the client.
- Read the current `run-id` from the `ZEALT_RUN_ID` environment variable and append it to the bucket name and ID so the task is safe to run concurrently.
- Refer to the Appwrite docs:
  - https://appwrite.io/docs/references/cloud/server-nodejs/storage#createBucket
  - https://appwrite.io/docs/products/storage/buckets
- The newer SDK style uses a single options object: `storage.createBucket({ bucketId, name, permissions, fileSecurity, maximumFileSize, allowedFileExtensions, compression, encryption, antivirus })`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Project path: /home/user/myproject
- Entry point: a Node.js script that can be executed by the verifier. The verifier will invoke it with `node /home/user/myproject/index.js`.
- The script reads `APPWRITE_ENDPOINT`, `APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID`, `APPWRITE_API_KEY`, and `ZEALT_RUN_ID` from environment variables.
- When the script runs successfully, a Storage bucket exists in the configured Appwrite project whose ID matches the value the script printed to stdout.
- The created bucket must satisfy ALL of:
  - `name` equals `secure-uploads-${run-id}` (where `run-id` is read from `ZEALT_RUN_ID`).
  - `fileSecurity` is `true`.
  - `maximumFileSize` equals `5242880`.
  - `allowedFileExtensions` is a set equal to `{"jpg", "jpeg", "png", "webp"}`.
  - `compression` equals `"gzip"`.
  - `encryption` is `true`.
  - `antivirus` is `true`.
  - `$permissions` contains both `read("users")` and `write("users")` (i.e., `Role.users()` for read and write).
- The final non-empty line of stdout must match the pattern: `BUCKET_ID: <bucket_id>`.

# Verification Plan

## Setup
- One-off job. Before running the solver, ensure no leftover bucket with the same ID exists from a prior aborted run (best-effort delete; ignore 404).

## Verification Steps
1. Read `run-id` from the `ZEALT_RUN_ID` environment variable. Expected bucket name = `secure-uploads-${run-id}`.
2. Execute the solver: `node /home/user/myproject/index.js`. The process must exit with code 0.
3. Parse stdout to extract the last line that matches `^BUCKET_ID:\s*(\S+)$`. Capture the captured group as `bucket_id`.
4. Using the Appwrite REST API (or `node-appwrite`) with `APPWRITE_ENDPOINT`, `APPWRITE_PROJECT_ID`, and `APPWRITE_API_KEY`, call `GET /storage/buckets/{bucket_id}` and verify the response body satisfies all of:
   - `name == "secure-uploads-${run-id}"`
   - `fileSecurity == true`
   - `maximumFileSize == 5242880`
   - `set(allowedFileExtensions) == {"jpg", "jpeg", "png", "webp"}`
   - `compression == "gzip"`
   - `encryption == true`
   - `antivirus == true`
   - `$permissions` contains both `read("users")` and `write("users")`.
5. Cleanup: regardless of pass/fail, delete the bucket via `DELETE /storage/buckets/{bucket_id}` (ignore 404).
